claims.text: Machine learning models can exhibit discrimination against minority groups in decision-making processes.
In-processing methods incorporate fairness directly during model design to induce intrinsically fair models.
In-processing fairness mitigation techniques can be categorized into explicit and implicit methods based on where fairness is achieved.
Explicit in-processing methods directly incorporate fairness metrics into training objectives.
Implicit in-processing methods focus on refining latent representation learning.

evidence.description: the models could show discrimination against minority groups and result in fairness issues in a decision-making process
fairness is directly taken into consideration during model design to induce intrinsically fair models
Based on where the fairness is achieved in the model, we categorize them into explicit and implicit methods
the former directly incorporates fairness metrics in training objectives
and the latter focuses on refining latent representation learning

future_work.text: Addressing key research challenges in in-processing machine learning fairness mitigation.
